title: The cloud-wave budget test fails intermittently under CI load
description:
FOUND 2026-09-23 on PR #38's CI: run-workflow.test.ts > 'a cloud wave in flight answers to a stop and to a budget > stops dispatching further batches once the cost budget is spent' FAILED on the CI runner. The same commit's re-run passed; main's CI on the same code passed; the whole file passed 88/88 three times locally. #38 changed only .github/workflows/ci.yml.

So it is load- or timing-dependent - the same class as owf (the epic-reconciler lease-lapse test). Per the flaky-means-bug rule it is a defect: a test that samples a condition it should wait for, or races wall time. Reproduce it deterministically (under CPU contention or with the fake clock pinned) before changing anything; do not raise a timeout to make it pass.
notes:
2026-09-23 11:44 - ESCALATED 2026-09-23, and now P1: this flake class is BLOCKING EPIC CLOSE-OUTS, not just colouring PRs. wne's close-out stopped twice on CI red; the second time six tests in one block all hit their 15s timeout together on the CI runner (run 35837696840: 'shows a cloud run live, with per-tick state and substrate-shaped sources', 'reports the durable verdict...', 'carries the gateway's cost on the closing event...', 'publishes no cost at all when the gateway telemetry could not be read', 'completes and collects identically when every event is dropped', 'streams the Phase 1 single-orchestrator run too...'), while a second CI run on the same head passed. Two aggravators: close-out requires EVERY check green, and since #38 each epic head gets TWO CI runs (push + pull_request), doubling the exposure. These tests wait on wall time with fixed deadlines against a simulated Workflow engine, so a slow runner fails them. Same class as owf. Belongs with t8u (deterministic contention).
2026-09-23 16:24 - INVESTIGATION, 2026-09-23, recorded straight so the next person does not repeat it.

ESTABLISHED:
  - The failing block ('a run streams run_event to the board') passes ALONE under heavy CPU contention (~1.6x slower, nowhere near 15s). A test that runs in 56ms locally hit 15s on CI - so on CI it was WAITING on something, not slow.
  - The whole file under contention (load ~110) failed once, on a different test ('does not redo work that already landed while the supervisor was dying', 58s).
  - An A/B under a load of ~30-40 did NOT discriminate: the unmodified file passed too. The failure is probabilistic; single loaded runs prove nothing either way.

DISPROVED: that a finished run's finalize addresses the NEXT test's fake sandboxes after its row goes terminal. A deterministic test showed it does not - its teardown was already done. (I had called this confirmed from reading the code before testing it; it was wrong.)

UNRESOLVED: what the stuck tests are waiting on.

DONE instead: firstProcess and settled now say what they saw when they time out - booted sandboxes and process counts; the run's row state and Workflow status (PR 'test: a timed-out wait ... says what it saw'). The NEXT CI failure names its cause; start there. Meanwhile each such failure on an epic head can be re-run, since the same head has repeatedly passed on a second run.
2026-09-23 20:55 - Mechanism found from the #40 diagnostics: a test ending with its run still stopping left a live Workflow booting containers into the next test's FakeSandboxes; firstProcess watched booted[0] (a stranger, 0 procs) and the failure cascaded. Fixed in #43 (afterEach terminates leaked Workflows; firstProcess ignores earlier tests' sandboxes). 89/89 locally, 4 concurrent runs green, CI green. Reopen if any run-workflow timeout recurs - the describer output will say which run.
acceptance_criteria: The failure is reproduced deterministically and its cause named; the test no longer depends on wall time or scheduling under load; the file passes repeatedly under induced CPU contention
